source: UNOOSA National Space Law database and official legislation portals / gazettes (verified 24 September 2026)

US.instrument: Commercial Space Launch Act 1984, as amended (51 U.S.C. ch. 509; FAA launch/re-entry licensing, 14 CFR Part 450); NOAA remote sensing licensing (51 U.S.C. ch. 601); FCC under Communications Act 1934

CIS.instrument: Law of the Russian Federation No. 5663-1 of 20 August 1993 "On Space Activities" (as amended)

PRC.instrument: Measures for the Administration of Registration of Objects Launched into Outer Space (2001); Interim Measures on the Administration of Permits for Civil Space Launch Projects (2002); no national Space Law

UK.instrument: Outer Space Act 1986 (UK entities' activities overseas) and Space Industry Act 2018 (activities in the UK; amended by Space Industry (Indemnities) Act 2025), with Space Industry Regulations 2021

JPN.instrument: Act on Launching of Spacecraft, etc. and Control of Spacecraft (Act No. 76 of 2016), amended by Act No. 39 of 2026; under the Basic Space Act (Act No. 43 of 2008)

FR.instrument: Law No. 2008-518 of 3 June 2008 on Space Operations (LOS), as amended, with Decree No. 2009-643 on authorisations

IND.instrument: No space act in force; IN-SPACe authorises private activity under the non-statutory Indian Space Policy 2023; spectrum under Telecommunications Act 2023. Space Activities Bill redrafted 2025, not introduced

ITSO.instrument: ITSO Agreement (1971, in force 1973; restructured 2001); privatised Intelsat fleet now owned by SES (acquired July 2025), satellites licensed mainly by the US FCC

ESA.instrument: Convention for the Establishment of a European Space Agency (signed Paris 30 May 1975, in force 30 October 1980); intergovernmental organisation, no single national supervising law

IT.instrument: Law No. 89 of 13 June 2025 on the space economy (authorisation of space activities); also Law No. 23/1983 (Liability Convention), Law No. 153/2005 (registration), Law No. 7/2018

GER.instrument: Satellite Data Security Act (SatDSiG) 2007, licensing high-grade Earth remote sensing systems; Space Tasks Transfer Act (RAÜG, 1990/1998). No general space act: draft Weltraumgesetz still in ministerial review

GLOB.instrument: Globalstar, Inc., US commercial operator (Delaware corp., Covington, Louisiana), system licensed by the US FCC; acquisition by Amazon agreed April 2026, pending approvals

CA.instrument: Remote Sensing Space Systems Act (S.C. 2005, c. 45) licenses remote sensing satellites; no launch licensing law yet (Canadian Space Launch Act, Bill C-28, at 2nd reading); Radiocommunication Act

SES.instrument: SES S.A., Betzdorf, Luxembourg; authorised under Luxembourg Law of 15 December 2020 on Space Activities (US-licensed satellites via FCC; incl. ex-Intelsat fleet since 2025)

SKOR.instrument: Space Development Promotion Act (Act No. 7538, 2005, as amended incl. 2024 KASA amendments) and Space Liability Act (Act No. 8714, 2007)

EUTE.instrument: Eutelsat S.A. (Paris area, France; privatised from EUTELSAT IGO); operations authorised under French Space Operations Act 2008 (OneWeb fleet under UK Outer Space Act 1986)

SPN.instrument: Royal Decree 278/1995 creates only a space-object registry; no space-activities licensing law (draft Space Activities Law under preparation by the Spanish Space Agency since 2025)

ORB.instrument: US commercial operator (ORBCOMM); Little LEO system licensed by the FCC under the Communications Act of 1934 since 1994 (OG2 replenishment authorised 2008, DA 08-633); US is the licensing State

AUS.instrument: Space (Launches and Returns) Act 2018 (formerly Space Activities Act 1998, renamed and amended by the Space Activities Amendment (Launches and Returns) Act 2018)

TURK.instrument: No space activities licensing law; Turkish Space Agency established by Presidential Decree No. 23 (Official Gazette 30624, 13 Dec 2018); satellite communications regulated under Electronic Communications Law No. 5809

ARGN.instrument: No comprehensive space activities act; CONAE created by Decree No. 995/1991; National Registry of Objects Launched into Outer Space by Decree No. 125/1995; spectrum licensed by ENACOM

ROC.instrument: Space Development Act (promulgated 16 June 2021, in force 20 January 2022; amended 28 June 2023)

O3B.instrument: SES S.A. subsidiary (O3b Limited, Jersey; SES HQ Luxembourg); O3b and O3b mPOWER satellites registered with the UN by the United Kingdom (e.g. ST/SG/SER.E/909, 2019; ST/SG/SER.E/1092, 2023)

NOR.instrument: Act of 22 December 2025 No. 128 relating to activities in outer space (the Space Act), in force 1 July 2026; repealed Act No. 38 of 1969

ISRA.instrument: No dedicated space legislation; an Israeli Space Law (licensing, supervision, liability) is in advanced inter-ministerial drafting (LSC 2026); satellite communications licensed under the Communications Law 1982

BRAZ.instrument: Law No. 14,946 of 31 July 2024 establishing rules for national space activities (General Space Law); AEB created by Law No. 8,854/1994

UAE.instrument: Federal Decree-Law No. 46 of 2023 on the Regulation of the Space Sector (replacing Federal Law No. 12 of 2019)

INDO.instrument: Law No. 21 of 2013 on Space Activities (Keantariksaan)

IM.instrument: Former IGO, privatised 1999, Viasat subsidiary since 2023 (HQ London); satellites licensed under the UK Outer Space Act 1986 and registered with the UN by the United Kingdom

SING.instrument: No space legislation yet; non-binding 2024 Guidelines for Singapore-Related Space Activities and national registry; National Space Agency (from 1 April 2026) mandated to develop a space law

AB.instrument: Intergovernmental organisation under the Agreement of the Arab Corporation for Space Communications (ARABSAT), Cairo 1976, amended 1990; League of Arab States depositary; HQ Riyadh

GREC.instrument: Law 4508/2017 on Authorisation of Space Activities, Registration in the National Register of Space Objects and Establishment of a Greek Space Organisation, amended by Law 4712/2020

SAUD.instrument: No space law enacted: draft Space Law and implementing regulations prepared; CST 'Space Sector Regulations and Guidelines' in consultation (Dec 2025); space regulated by CST under its Ordinance (amended 2024)

EGYP.instrument: No space-activities licensing law; Law No. 3 of 2018 establishes the Egyptian Space Agency (agency statute only). Satellite services licensed by NTRA under Telecommunication Regulation Law No. 10 of 2003

POL.instrument: Act of 13 February 2026 on Space Activities (Dz.U. 2026 poz. 465; in force 18 April 2026): authorisation, supervision, liability, national register of space objects

EUME.instrument: Convention for the Establishment of EUMETSAT (1983; in force 1986; amended 2000). EUMETSAT has declared acceptance of the Rescue, Liability and Registration Conventions and registers its own satellites with the UN

THAI.instrument: No space act in force. Draft Space Affairs Act (Cabinet-approved 2021) still unenacted; Council of State review (2025), and the National Space Policy Committee ordered it revised in Aug 2026

MALA.instrument: Malaysian Space Board Act 2022 (Act 834), gazetted 25 January 2022; fully in force since 1 January 2025

LUXE.instrument: Law of 15 December 2020 on Space Activities; also Law of 20 July 2017 on the Exploration and Use of Space Resources

PAKI.instrument: Pakistan Space Activities Rules, 2024 (S.R.O. 60(I)/2024, 1 Feb 2024), made under the National Command Authority Act 2010; establish the Pakistan Space Activities Regulatory Board (PSARB)

IRAN.instrument: No comprehensive space act. Statute of the Iranian Space Agency (Cabinet, 2005; revised 2008), under the 2003 Law on Duties and Powers of the ICT Ministry, lets the agency authorise space activities

MEX.instrument: No space-activities licensing law; Ley que Crea la Agencia Espacial Mexicana (DOF 30 July 2010) creates the agency. Satellite/orbital use authorised under the Ley en Materia de Telecomunicaciones y Radiodifusión (DOF 16 July 2025)

BEL.instrument: Law of 17 September 2005 on the activities of launching, flight operations or guidance of space objects (amended by Law of 1 December 2013); Royal Decree of 15 March 2022

DEN.instrument: Act No. 409 of 11 May 2016 on Activities in Outer Space (Outer Space Act); Executive Order No. 1116 of 3 June 2021

NATO.instrument: Intergovernmental military alliance (North Atlantic Treaty 1949); no national space law of its own. NATO IV satellites were supervised and registered via the United Kingdom

AC.instrument: Hong Kong-incorporated commercial operator licensed under Hong Kong's Outer Space Ordinance (Cap. 523, 1997); China is the State of registry for its satellites

ABS.instrument: Commercial operator (ABS Global Ltd, formerly Bermuda-domiciled; Outer Space Act 1986 (Bermuda) Order 2006). Redomiciled to Dubai, UAE, Oct 2025 as Agility Beyond Space; current supervising State unconfirmed

ALG.instrument: Law No. 19-06 of 17 July 2019 on Space Activities (declares space activities a State monopoly; ASAL register of space objects)

SWTZ.instrument: No space act in force. Draft Federal Act on Space Operations (Raumfahrtgesetz) sent to Parliament 25 Feb 2026; National Council adopted it 24 Sept 2026 (191-0); Council of States still to decide

NETH.instrument: Space Activities Act (Wet ruimtevaartactiviteiten) of 24 January 2007, as amended (incl. 2015 extension to non-manoeuvrable satellites)

POR.instrument: Decree-Law No. 16/2019 of 22 January (Space Activities regime), as amended by Decree-Law No. 20/2024 of 2 February (incl. spaceport licensing)

RWA.instrument: Law N° 022/2021 of 18/04/2021 establishing Rwanda Space Agency (RSA), Art. 8: power to issue and follow up permits, authorisations and licences for space activities

CZCH.instrument: No space activities act (drafting discussed, none enacted by Sept 2026); Ministry of Transport coordinates space activities; satellite radio frequencies licensed under Electronic Communications Act No. 127/2005

UKR.instrument: Law of Ukraine 'On Space Activity' No. 502/96-VR of 15 November 1996, as amended (incl. Law No. 1089-IX of 2020)

KAZ.instrument: Law of the Republic of Kazakhstan No. 528-IV of 6 January 2012 'On Space Activity', as amended

CHBZ.instrument: China-Brazil Earth Resources Satellite (CBERS) joint programme (1988 protocol); objects registered nationally, e.g. CBERS-4A by Brazil (ST/SG/SER.E/927). See PRC and BRAZ entries

NIG.instrument: National Space Research and Development Agency Act 2010 (Act No. 9 of 2010), s. 9: licensing of space activities by the National Space Council

BUL.instrument: No space activities act (earlier licensing bill not enacted); Ministry of Innovation and Growth coordinates space policy; satellite frequencies regulated under the Electronic Communications Act

VTNM.instrument: No national space law; space development guided by Decision No. 169/QD-TTg (2021) space S&T strategy to 2030; satellites regulated under the Law on Radio Frequencies and Law on Telecommunications

AZER.instrument: Law of the Republic of Azerbaijan No. 927-VIQ of 24 June 2023 'On Space Activities'

BELA.instrument: No space activities (licensing) law; Presidential Decree No. 609 of 22 Dec 2004 (amended by Decree No. 403, 2011) tasks the National Academy of Sciences with space policy coordination and regulation

MA.instrument: No national space activities law; state programmes run by the Royal Centre for Remote Sensing (CRTS) and CRERS; satellite spectrum regulated by ANRT under Law No. 24-96 on post and telecommunications

HUN.instrument: No space activities act in force: government began drafting a space law in March 2025, not adopted; satellite frequencies licensed by NMHH under Act C of 2003 on Electronic Communications

RP.instrument: Philippine Space Act (Republic Act No. 11363, 2019) creates PhilSA, space policy and a national registry, but no authorisation/licensing regime for non-governmental space activities

CHLE.instrument: No space activities law; governance via Law No. 21.105 (2018), Supreme Decree No. 24 (2021) on space policy bodies and Decree No. 30 (2024) National Space Policy; satellites licensed under Telecom Law 18.168

SAFR.instrument: Space Affairs Act No. 84 of 1993, as amended by the Space Affairs Amendment Act No. 64 of 1995

VENZ.instrument: Law on the Bolivarian Agency for Space Activities (ABAE), Official Gazette No. 38.796 of 25 Oct 2007: agency statute without an authorisation/licensing regime for space activities

ASRA.instrument: Federal Law on the Authorisation of Space Activities and the Establishment of a National Space Registry (Austrian Outer Space Act), BGBl. I No. 132/2011, as amended by BGBl. I No. 37/2018

FGER.instrument: Franco-German Symphonie communications satellite programme (Symphonie 1-2, 1974-75), reported to the UN by both FR Germany and France. See FR (Space Operations Act 2008) and GER entries

STCT.instrument: ST-1 (1998) and ST-2 (2011), joint SingTel/Chunghwa Telecom satellites; not UN-registered. Taiwan: Space Development Act 2021 (am. 2023); Singapore: no space licensing law

RASC.instrument: RASCOM Convention (Regional African Satellite Communication Organization, est. 1992-93, HQ Abidjan, 45 signatory States); satellites operated by RascomStar-QAF Ltd (Mauritius company) under RASCOM concession; not UN-registered

ECU.instrument: No space licensing law. Exec. Decree 1246 (2012) created Ecuadorian Space Institute, abolished by Exec. Decree 714 (2019); Exec. Decree 143 (2025) gives space R&D to the Air Force; satellites under Organic Telecoms Law 2015

PERU.instrument: No comprehensive licensing law. Decree-Law No. 20643 (1974) creates CONIDA; Supreme Decree No. 008-2016-DE creates National Registry of Space Objects; Law 32571 (2026) declares a spaceport of national interest

FRIT.instrument: Franco-Italian govt satcom cooperation (CNES/ASI, defence ministries): Athena-Fidus registered by France, SICRAL 2 by Italy. France: Space Operations Act 2008-518; Italy: Law 89/2025 on the space economy

ANG.instrument: No national space law; GGPEN created by Presidential Decree 154/13, organic statute Presidential Decree 152/21 (agency only); satellite services under electronic communications law

SVN.instrument: Space Activities Act (ZVDej), Official Gazette RS No. 43/2022; Decree on the implementation of the Space Activities Act (2022)

LTU.instrument: No dedicated space activities law (none adopted or tabled as of Sept 2026); satellite radio matters under Law on Electronic Communications No. IX-2135 (2004, as amended)

KWT.instrument: No national space activities law identified; Law No. 37 of 2014 establishes CITRA (general telecom regulator), not a space-specific law

ISS.instrument: Agreement Concerning Cooperation on the Civil International Space Station (IGA), 29 Jan 1998, among US, Russia, Japan, Canada and ESA member States; each partner registers its own elements (Art. 5)

SEAL.instrument: Sea Launch consortium (Boeing, RSC Energia, Kvaerner, Yuzhnoye/Yuzhmash); Zenit-3SL launches from the Odyssey sea platform were licensed by the US FAA/AST under 51 U.S.C. ch. 509

NICO.instrument: Commercial operator code: sole object ICO F2 (2001-026A), registered by the United States (ST/SG/SER.E/400); now operated by Omnispace LLC as OMNI-M1; see US entry

USBZ.instrument: Sole object Estrela do Sul 1 (Loral/Telesat Brasil), registered by Brazil (ST/SG/SER.E/678); launched by Sea Launch under US FAA licence (51 U.S.C. ch. 509); see US and BRAZ entries

COL.instrument: No space licensing law. Decree 2442 of 2006 creates the Colombian Space Commission (amended by Decree 184 of 2023); satellites under ICT Law 1341 of 2009; 2025 AESCOL agency bill not enacted

EST.instrument: No space act in force. Draft Space Act (Kosmoseseadus, EIS dossier 24-0963) consulted 2024 and submitted to the Government Aug 2026, not yet adopted; radio spectrum under Electronic Communications Act

BOL.instrument: No space licensing law. Supreme Decree No. 0423 (2010) creates the Bolivian Space Agency (ABE); satellite services under General Telecommunications/ICT Law No. 164 of 2011

URY.instrument: No space activities law. 2022 bill for a Uruguayan Space Agency not enacted; a 101-article space policy bill was announced Sept 2026 but not yet in Parliament; satellites regulated by URSEC

IRAQ.instrument: No national space law; satellite services licensed by the Communications and Media Commission under CPA Order No. 65 (2004), incl. Regulations for licensing terrestrial stations for space services (2024)

TMMC.instrument: Joint TürkmenÄlem 52°E/MonacoSAT (2015): Turkmen-operated satellite at Monaco's ITU orbital slot. Turkmenistan: Law No. 307-V On Space Activities (2015, amended 2017, 2018); Monaco: no space act yet (draft)

LAOS.instrument: No dedicated space act; satellites regulated under the Law on Telecommunications (2011) and Decree on Satellite Communications No. 471/GOL (2019), administered by the telecoms ministry

BGD.instrument: No dedicated space act; satellite services licensed by BTRC under the Bangladesh Telecommunication Act 2001 (Act No. XVIII of 2001, as amended)

JOR.instrument: No dedicated space act; satellite and spectrum licensing by the Telecommunications Regulatory Commission under Telecommunications Law No. 13 of 1995 (as amended)

GRSA.instrument: Hellas Sat 4/SaudiGeoSat-1 (2019), shared by Arabsat's Hellas Sat and KACST; registered by Greece, licensing State under Law 4508/2017 on licensing of space activities

ETH.instrument: No space activities licensing law; SSGI established under Proclamation No. 1263/2021 (Art. 57(1)) with powers set by Council of Ministers Regulation No. 511/2022; National Space Policy

NKOR.instrument: Law of the DPRK on Space Development (Supreme People's Assembly, 1 April 2013; revised by SPA Standing Committee 7 August 2022, adding defence purposes)

SVK.instrument: Act No. 378/2024 Coll. on the regulation of space activities (and amending Act No. 145/1995 Coll. on administrative fees), 28 November 2024

HRV.instrument: No dedicated space activities law; satellite networks and spectrum regulated by HAKOM under the Electronic Communications Act (NN 76/2022, as amended)

DJI.instrument: Law No. 167/AN/22/8ème L on launch, flight operation and guidance of space objects (10 Nov 2022); implementing Decree No. 2023-209/PR/MENSUR on authorisation procedure (2023)

BWA.instrument: No space law, space agency or space policy yet (in development); spectrum and satellite communications regulated by BOCRA under the Communications Regulatory Authority Act 2012

BHR.instrument: No enacted space law; National Space Law (licensing, liability) being developed by the Bahrain Space Agency (est. 2014 as NSSA, renamed 2025); spectrum handled by the TRA

SLB.instrument: No dedicated space act; satellite filings and spectrum administered by the Telecommunications Commission (TCSI) under the Telecommunications Act 2009

NZ.instrument: Outer Space and High-altitude Activities Act 2017 (as amended, incl. Amendment Act 2025 on ground-based space infrastructure); Licences and Permits Regulations 2017

MNE.instrument: No dedicated space act; satellite spectrum and communications regulated by EKIP under the Law on Electronic Communications (Official Gazette 100/24, as amended)

ROM.instrument: No space activities authorisation law; Law No. 380/2022 (accession to Registration Convention) tasks ROSA with setting up and keeping the national registry of space objects
